subsystems.name: Stimulus presentation
subsystems.role: presents visual patterns that trigger a repeatable brain response.

subsystems.name: EEG acquisition
subsystems.role: records the brain's electrical activity from the scalp.

subsystems.name: Signal conditioning
subsystems.role: cleans the raw signal and extracts relevant features.

subsystems.name: Template management
subsystems.role: stores each user's unique neural signature securely.

subsystems.name: Matching engine
subsystems.role: compares a live recording to stored templates and makes a decision.
parts: classifier (e.g. support vector machine, neural network)

subsystems.name: Presentation attack detection
subsystems.role: ensures a live person is present and prevents replay or synthetic signals.

buildSteps.title: Choose a stimulus protocol
buildSteps.detail: Select visual stimuli such as images of faces, objects or flickering patterns that evoke strong, consistent EEG responses. Test on volunteers to find the most discriminative set.

buildSteps.title: Design the headset
buildSteps.detail: Integrate dry or comfortable wet electrodes in a quick-to-don headset. Optimise electrode placement over visual areas of the brain and amplify signals with low noise.

buildSteps.title: Collect enrollment data
buildSteps.detail: Each user views the stimuli many times across several sessions. Record EEG with precise timing relative to each stimulus.

buildSteps.title: Preprocess the signals
buildSteps.detail: Filter out drift and noise, remove eye blinks and muscle artifacts, and segment the recording into short epochs around each stimulus.

buildSteps.title: Extract features
buildSteps.detail: Compute event-related potentials or spectral features from each epoch. Select features that are stable within a person but differ between people.

buildSteps.title: Train a classifier
buildSteps.detail: Use machine learning to build a model that maps features to identity. Validate with data from new sessions and new users.

buildSteps.title: Integrate into an access system
buildSteps.detail: Build a verification station with display and headset. The user undergoes a short session; real-time processing compares the signal to a stored template.

buildSteps.title: Add security and privacy measures
buildSteps.detail: Encrypt templates, enforce liveness, and allow revocation if a template is compromised. Test against spoofing and replay attacks.

prerequisites.why: dry electrode headsets exist, but signal quality and comfort for security use are still improving.
mature techniques can classify brain signals, but adapting them to robust authentication needs more data.
research shows EEG differs between people, yet the most stable and discriminative features are not fully standardised.
encryption and secure storage methods are well developed, though neural data raises new privacy questions.
no proven method guarantees a recorded signal comes from a live person rather than a replay or synthesis.

pathway.milestone: lab studies achieve high accuracy in small groups under controlled conditions
pathway.unlocks: proof that neural signatures can identify people.

pathway.milestone: dry-electrode headsets and shorter protocols enable pilot trials in high-security access
pathway.unlocks: real-world testing of usability and reliability.

pathway.milestone: fusion with other biometrics (fingerprint, face) to reduce error rates
pathway.unlocks: practical deployment where one modality fails.

pathway.milestone: continuous authentication from wearable or implanted sensors
pathway.unlocks: seamless, ongoing identity verification without explicit actions.
